subsystems.name: Fusion core
subsystems.role: creates and holds the fusing plasma that is the energy source.
parts: field-reversed configuration or compact torus plasma

subsystems.name: Magnetic nozzle
subsystems.role: the 'exhaust pipe': magnetic field lines guide charged fusion products out the back to make thrust.

subsystems.name: Fuel system
subsystems.role: stores and injects deuterium and helium-3 (or deuterium alone).

subsystems.name: Shielding and heat rejection
subsystems.role: protects structure and crew from neutrons while dumping waste heat.

subsystems.name: Power and control
subsystems.role: runs the magnets and controls the plasma, and in some concepts supplies ship electricity.

subsystems.name: Structure
subsystems.role: a very light frame that carries thrust loads without the thousands of tonnes of a ground tokamak.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate net gain in a compact core
buildSteps.detail: A drive only makes sense if the plasma produces more energy than it absorbs while weighing a small fraction of a ground experiment.

buildSteps.title: Choose a fuel that exhausts as charged particles
buildSteps.detail: Deuterium–helium-3 is favoured because most of its energy leaves as fast charged particles that a magnetic field can steer, rather than as neutrons that heat the ship. This is also its hardest problem: helium-3 is extremely scarce.

buildSteps.title: Wind lightweight superconducting coils
buildSteps.detail: High-temperature superconducting tape is wound into coils designed for high field per kilogram, since every tonne of coil is a tonne of payload lost.

buildSteps.title: Build and vacuum-test the magnetic nozzle
buildSteps.detail: The nozzle is tested in large vacuum chambers with plasma sources that approximate, but cannot fully reproduce, a real fusion exhaust.

buildSteps.title: Integrate shielding and radiators
buildSteps.detail: Neutron shielding and heat rejection are sized for the mission, then wrapped around the core.

buildSteps.title: Fire the integrated drive on the ground
buildSteps.detail: The complete article is run in a vacuum chamber long enough to measure thrust, specific impulse and thermal behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Fly a small demonstration spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: A compact uncrewed craft would start the core in orbit, fire briefly, and measure thrust against predictions.

buildSteps.title: Scale to crewed interplanetary missions
buildSteps.detail: Only after flight data exist would the design be enlarged for high-power, long-duration burns.

prerequisites.tech: Fusion reactors with net energy gain
prerequisites.why: inertial laser fusion reached gain in 2022, but no magnetic confinement device has yet produced net energy.
high-temperature superconducting coils now reach fields that shrink a reactor, but not yet at the mass a spacecraft needs.
there is no established source; proposed extraction from lunar soil or gas-giant atmospheres does not exist.

prerequisites.tech: Magnetic nozzle physics for fusion-grade plasma
prerequisites.why: directing a 100-million-degree exhaust has only been modelled and tested with much cooler plasmas.
a drive must survive neutron and heat loads with a fraction of the shielding used on the ground.

pathway.milestone: fusion core experiments on the ground, plus concept studies of field-reversed configurations for space
pathway.unlocks: the plasma physics and control algorithms a drive would need.
credible reactor cores that could in principle be miniaturised.

pathway.milestone: a space-based drive demonstration measuring real thrust from fusion products
pathway.unlocks: mission designers can plan around measured performance rather than models.

pathway.milestone: uncrewed high-power probes to the outer planets
pathway.unlocks: multi-month round trips and heavy science payloads instead of flybys.
fast transits with far less radiation exposure for crews — the scenario long studied by concepts such as Project Daedalus.
